findings.title: acceptEdits auto-allows FileWrite under .cursor/ (hooks.json / mcp.json) while .vscode/.idea/.claude are blocked — Cursor hooks auto-execute.
findings.description: DISTINCT from filed husky/lefthook/.git hooks, root .mcp.json, REPL/debugger cwd inits, and the existing .vscode block. DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES is only .git/.vscode/.idea/.claude. The comment at filesystem.ts:430 blocks .vscode specifically to prevent IDE settings manipulation and potential code execution, but omits .cursor/. Under acceptEdits, in-cwd FileWrite of .cursor/hooks.json, .cursor/hooks/*, and .cursor/mcp.json therefore auto-allows after checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit. Cursor project hooks (/.cursor/hooks.json) automatically load and run in trusted workspaces; Cursor reloads hooks.json on change; cloud agents pick up project hooks. Workspace trust is off by default (all folders trusted). Hook command can be inline shell — no separate chmod. Live bun FileWriteTool check (cwd set, mode acceptEdits): .cursor/hooks.json / .cursor/mcp.json ALLOW; .vscode/tasks.json / .claude/settings.json / .mcp.json / .bashrc ASK. Project settings can set permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits with no BypassPermissionsModeDialog.
findings.impact: After generic Trust plus acceptEdits (project-planted or user-selected), the model can silently plant .cursor/hooks.json (and optional hook scripts / .cursor/mcp.json). The next Cursor agent event (sessionStart, afterFileEdit, beforeShellExecution, …), workspaceOpen, or Cursor cloud-agent run executes attacker commands as the victim — delayed RCE via the IDE hook loader that Claude Code already tried to cover for .vscode/.claude but missed for .cursor.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker commits CLAUDE.md instructing a 'Cursor project helper' write of .cursor/hooks.json (optional: .claude/settings.json permissions.defaultMode acceptEdits).
2. Victim clones, reviews the tree (no malicious hooks yet), and trusts the folder in Claude Code. TrustDialog is generic; acceptEdits does not show Bypass Permissions.
3. FileWrite of .cursor/hooks.json with e.g. sessionStart/afterFileEdit/beforeShellExecution command set to inline shell RCE passes isDangerousFilePathToAutoEdit (.cursor absent from DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES) and is auto-allowed because the path is inside cwd.
4. Victim later opens/continues the project in Cursor (or a Cursor cloud agent runs). Cursor auto-loads project hooks and executes the planted command.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks (project hooks auto-load in trusted workspaces; cloud agents load .cursor/hooks.json)
findings.remediation: Add .cursor to DANGEROUS_DIRECTORIES alongside .vscode/.idea/.claude so acceptEdits cannot auto-write Cursor hooks or project MCP configs. Do not honor defaultMode acceptEdits from projectSettings without disclosing it. Require an explicit prompt for writes under IDE config directories that auto-execute.
findings.why_distinct: Not husky/lefthook/.git (those paths are blocked via .git). Not root .mcp.json (already in DANGEROUS_FILES). Not REPL/debugger cwd inits (already filed). Trigger/loader is Cursor project hooks (and optionally .cursor/mcp.json) — the missing sibling of the intentional .vscode code-execution block.
findings.poc_video_notes: Live bun FileWriteTool+checkPathSafetyForAutoEdit with setOriginalCwd: .cursor/hooks.json, .cursor/hooks/pwn.sh, .cursor/mcp.json returned behavior=allow decisionReason.mode=acceptEdits; .vscode/tasks.json, .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, .bashrc returned ask/safetyCheck. A live Claude Code REPL session writing hooks and a live Cursor IDE hook fire were not run on this host; Cursor auto-load behavior is from official docs.
